correctness.rationale: The statement concerns precisely the standard labeled twelve-vertex Frucht graph and ordinary matching complex. A complete signed integer boundary computation on all 1,025 nonempty simplices establishes ranks 17,100,233,144,8 with unimodular primitive boundary bases, yielding integral homology Z^20 only in degree 3. The proved minimal flag-support lemma forces eight vertices and an octahedral sphere. Exhaustive enumeration of four vertex-disjoint two-edge paths gives exactly 87 distinct induced carriers. Their 16-term signed fundamental chains all have zero boundary, remain nonzero and primitive after exact integral reduction mod im(partial_4), and 20 selected columns admit additional integer unit pivots; lattice saturation then implies these are an integral homology basis. Standalone complete and independent modular verifiers were executed from actual source files. No extrapolation from primes or partial enumeration is used.

value.rationale: This is the canonical smallest asymmetric cubic graph: a symmetry-free and nontrivial case for the local-to-global homological question of whether minimally supported induced spherical cycles generate ambient integral homology. The 87 geometric carriers are natural spanning P3-factor objects, not arbitrary subcomplex slices. Their nonzero primitive images and an explicit 20-class integral basis distinguish integral generation from the abstract Betti count or general cross-polytope shapes; these are not immediate textbook consequences of known connectivity or homotopy-type results. The finite classification fully answers a motivated exact natural invariant without claiming an unjustified family extension.
